mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing wage growth and consumer spending, which in turn depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) signals a restrictive monetary policy environment that suppresses demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising AND RSAFS falling for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS rises and RSAFS falls for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average combined with a concurrent increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates labor market churning, which may precede earnings downgrades and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average AND UNRATE > previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of labor market churning as defined.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during five consecutive months of HOUST above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both GDPC1 and INDPRO above their 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals broad-based demand and supply expansion, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-month moving average AND INDPRO > 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during three consecutive months of both GDPC1 and INDPRO above their 12-month moving averages.
